newsitem.title: USA: CBOT old crop corn ends down on commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT old crop corn ends down on commercial selling.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed on Thursday with nearby old crop contracts lower on commercial hedge selling, traders said.
"There was good farmer selling in the country and corn is going to break," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Cargill Inc reportedly sold at least two million bushels March and Term Commodities sold two million July.
But new crop months closed firm as funds bought at least 15 million bushels. Refco Inc, Dean Witter, Prudential Securities and Rosenthal Collins were among the buyers.
Traders attributed some of the new crop buying interest to a narrowing of the spread between new crop November soybeans and December corn.

When the spread widens beyond 2.4 to 1.0, premium soybeans, farmers tend to plant more acreage to soybeans at the expense of corn because profit margins are better, traders said. The spread closed Thursday at 2.55 to 1.0, compared with 2.62 to 1.0 on Monday.
Corn closed 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher with March down 1/4 at $2.73-1/2 a bushel and December up one at $2.69-3/4.
In options, Continental Grain bought 1,400 $2.60 March puts at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 cents per bushel, traders said. Refco Inc bought 700 March $2.60 calls at 14-1/2 to 15 cents.
Volume was estimated at 55,000 contracts, against Wednesday's actual volume of 66,186 contracts.
